messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 05 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Region pinning follow-up and next steps

Hi Samir 	6

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and a short list of follow-ups so we can get a scoped proposal over to you: 

Key points we captured:
- Primary requirement: customer data (PII + inference inputs/outputs) must remain in EU data centers.
- App-level routing: traffic should be pinned to EU region for all production inference traffic, with an automated cross-region failover only for DR (non-active-active).
- Backups: Acme wants nightly backups retained in the EU for 90 days; DR replica can be in US only if encrypted and approved by Acme.
- Logging/audit: Access logs and request metadata needed for 90-day retention; full request payload logging is restricted and must be configurable.
- KMS/BYOK: preference for customer-managed keys in their AWS account.

Action items we promised:
1) Send the region-pinning architecture diagram + short whitepaper on EU residency (attached).
2) Confirm whether Redwood supports BYOK for both hosted and dedicated flows.
3) Clarify cross-region failover behavior (active-active vs active-passive) and what controls are available.
4) Provide an initial estimate of any uplift in cost and SLA implications for the pinned deployment.

I've attached the preliminary region_pinning_design.pdf and our region-pinning whitepaper. Aditya and Marissa are cc'd 	6 they will handle the technical answers and the cost/SLA estimate.

Proposed next step: 30-minute technical follow-up next week to walk through the diagram and verify the backup/DR approach. Please suggest a time that works for your infra/security team.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: region_pinning_design.pdf, redwood-region-pinning-whitepaper.pdf

From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acmebank.com>

Cc: Laila Ortiz <laila.ortiz@acmebank.com>, Damien O'Neill <damien.oneill@acmebank.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Apr 2028 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Region pinning follow-up and next steps

Vanessa 	6

Thanks for the summary and the attachments. A few clarifications from our side so the follow-up can be more concrete: 

1) EU residency 
- All inference inputs and outputs (including temporary KV cache contents) must be stored and processed in the EU. No copy of PII can be stored outside the EU except for a DR scenario that has been pre-approved.

2) Backups and DR 
- Nightly backups must be retained in the EU for a minimum of 90 days. DR replicas are acceptable in the US only if: (a) encryption in transit and at rest is enforced, (b) we have a signed Data Transfer Addendum that specifies controls, and (c) the failover plan requires manual authorization from Acme Security.

3) Logging and auditing 
- We need configurable request logging. By default we will log metadata only; full payload logging can be enabled per-route with a compliance review.

4) KMS/BYOK 
- Acme requires BYOK with keys managed in our AWS account (not Redwood-managed) for any crypto operations tied to PII.

Can your team confirm the above constraints are possible and, if so, outline any trade-offs? Also include any changes to SLA (RPO/RTO) and cost for the pinned EU-only deployment. If possible, we will include this as part of our risk assessment for the procurement team.

I attached our internal requirements spreadsheet (acme_data_requirements.xlsx).

Best,
Samir Khan
Head of Platform Security, Acme Bank
samir.khan@acmebank.com

Attachments: acme_data_requirements.xlsx

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acmebank.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 05 Apr 2028 13:18:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Region pinning follow-up and next steps

Hi Samir 	6

Thanks for the clear requirements and the spreadsheet 	6 very helpful. Short answers to your points and a few implementation notes: 

1) EU residency and processing
- Supported: Redwood can pin inference processing and persistent storage (including KV caches) to EU regions. For hosted EU deployments we guarantee processing and storage in the selected EU region under the region-pinning config.

2) Backups and DR
- Nightly backups retained in the EU for 90 days: supported.
- Cross-region DR: we support an active-passive failover model. The passive replica can be stored in the US but will remain encrypted and access-restricted. Failover to the US replica requires manual approval (we can automate the approval workflow but it must be triggered by an authorized Acme identity).
- Note: Active-active across EU/US is not available for low-latency inference given current KV/cache consistency constraints.

3) Logging and audit controls
- Configurable logging per-route: by default only non-sensitive metadata is logged. Full request payload logging is available but must be enabled explicitly and will be flagged in our compliance reports. Logs can be retained in EU-only storage endpoints as required.

4) KMS/BYOK
- BYOK is supported for both hosted and dedicated deployments. For hosted we can integrate with your AWS KMS key via an exfiltration-restricted key policy and dedicated HSM-backed wraps for additional controls. For dedicated we can also support customer-managed HSM.

5) SLA / RTO / RPO trade-offs
- With region pinning and manual DR failover: target RTO is ~2 hours (manual authorization + warm-up). RPO is nightly backups (up to 24 hours). If Acme requires sub-hour RPO or automated cross-region failover we will need an architecture change to active-replica streaming which has cost and latency trade-offs. I'll include rough cost deltas in the formal estimate.

Next steps:
- I will attach a short tech note and a tentative cost uplift matrix. Can we schedule a 30-minute call next Tue (Apr 10) with your platform/security folks to walk the design and sign off on the DR manual failover flow?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0199

Per Aditya's notes: we can meet the EU residency and backup retention requirements, support BYOK, and offer manual cross-region failover to a US passive replica under the conditions you outlined. The trade-offs are: no active-active low-latency multi-region inference, and RPO will be nightly unless you opt into streaming replication (higher cost).

Proposed next steps:
- Schedule a 30-min technical review Tue Apr 10 at 10:00 AM BST / 05:00 AM EDT (I know timezones are tight 	6 happy to move). Please confirm if this works for Acme Security and Platform (Samir, Laila, Damien).
- We will send the technical_note_region_pinning.pdf and a cost uplift matrix by EOD today so you can share with procurement.
- If the manual failover approach is acceptable, we will draft the Data Transfer Addendum and the technical annex for BYOK to include in the SOW.

If you confirm the meeting time I'll send a calendar invite and the join link. Looking forward to getting this over the line.

Thanks,
Vanessa
